Source: Der Rebbe Redt Tzu Kinder, New Edition (Vol. 3, pp. 168-169); Sicha

I just came back from the funnest and most interesting Shabbos sleepover at Mussie’s house. Before Shabbos, we turned on the lamp in her room so we could party until the morning. We played every card game and board game in her closet and finished all the snacks in the pantry, before falling asleep right in the middle of the bedroom rug. Oh well, so much for a whole night of fun.

The biggest surprise came when I woke up. Shabbos morning at my house always includes Mommy’s delicious brownies and a bowl of cereal so sweet and colorful that it turns my milk purple. So I had been wondering what Mussie’s house would be like.

Well, let’s just start by saying that I didn’t expect her to wake

up before me. But she did. Plus, she was already dressed! In a loud whisper, she announced that she was going downstairs to learn a maamar. I must have given her a weird look, because she quickly added, “Don’t you ever learn Chassidus with your father?”

I decided to join them, and that ended up being the best part of the whole Shabbos. We drank tea and

Mussie’s father said it was something that usually only adults get to learn, because it’s full of difficult ideas. I didn’t understand a lot, but

my plans to become a five- star general and blast away

This morning, our whole school drove to Crown Heights to join the greatest Great Parade ever. We all marched with our uniforms, banners, and heads held high while everyone cheered us on. And as we passed by 770, I could picture the Rebbe waving to us with a huge smile.

Oh—and three news reporters stopped us for photos of our poster.

After the parade, I met my family at Bubby’s house on Crown Street. I thought back to the Shabbos morning maamar at Mussie’s, and I asked Bubby if she ever learned with her father when she was young. Bubby laughed. She said that in her days, young girls didn’t learn much Chassidus. But now, because we’re coming closer to the times of Moshiach, things are changing.

On the day that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai (also known as Rashbi) was going to pass away, his students gathered around his bed. Rashbi showed them the parts of Torah that are like sparkling treasures buried deep in the ground. They had never heard such wonderful Torah secrets before. Rashbi spoke for a long time, teaching his talmidim many new explanations of Torah.

Rashbi said that this would happen again one day. Right before Moshiach comes, many people will study the secrets of Torah—including children. That’s how they’ll bring Moshiach closer.

that when Moshiach comes, we’ll get to dig up the hidden treasures of Torah.

This Shabbos morning at 8:00, I heard Tatty learning in his musical voice. I tiptoed down the stairs and knocked on the door of his office.

Tatty was happy to see me. “You’re up early,” he said with a smile.

“Could I learn some Chassidus with you?” I asked right away.

Tatty stroked his beard. “This is a difficult maamar,” he explained.

Tatty turned a few pages, looking through the words and thinking.

“Tatty,” I said, “Bubby told me that us kids are going to bring Moshiach through learning the secrets of the Torah!”

Finally, Tatty invited me to come sit next to him, and we learned the maamar together.

See? The secrets of the Torah are becoming secrets no more, now that we’re getting super-duper close to Moshiach’s times. I bet when Hashem finally takes us out of Golus, it won’t even be hard to understand Chassidus anymore. Kids will share a maamar as easily as we share our snacks.

I can’t wait to learn again with Tatty next Shabbos. And I can’t wait till Moshiach comes and the world will be filled with the treasures of Rashbi.
